criteria.effective_rank_improvement_rule: effective rank (RankMe): convolutional improves >=5% over next-best, across-seed CI of the improvement above 5%.
criteria.shuffled_reference_role: Shuffled references are used only in the single-seed measurements to check for leakage and probe behavior; they are not comparison baselines.
criteria.signal_rule: For each tokenizer and target, the prediction score exceeds the manual-indicator baseline when the across-seed CI of (tokenizer - indicators) excludes 0.
criteria.windows: Training, validation, and test results are recorded in per_tokenizer[tokenizer].windows; the criteria below apply to held-out test data.

indicator_baseline.source: Manual-indicator baseline: RidgeCV predicts each target from the 12 indicator variables; each tokenizer is compared with this baseline.

across_seed_results.note: Across-seed measurements for the 5-seed encoder experiment. Training, validation, and test results are recorded in per_tokenizer[tokenizer].windows. The recorded criteria require >=5% improvement over the next-best tokenizer and prediction scores above the indicator baseline on held-out test data. Only seed 4395 is released; recomputing its measurements requires its checkpoints and the original corpus. Recomputing the full comparison requires all 5 seeds and the licensed corpus.

indicator_comparison.method: Original targets; raw anchor indicators; train-only scaling; five chronological whole-day ridge-validation folds; paired whole-day percentile bootstrap and independent seed resampling within each tokenizer.
indicator_comparison.limitations: Conditional on the training dataset and fitted encoders. Five seeds. Exploratory evaluation on the same test period; target-wise intervals are not multiplicity-adjusted. Rank-IC percentage margins require a positive comparator. R² differences and squared-error reductions are separate effect measures.

checkpoint_evaluation.ci_caveat: Day-block-bootstrap CIs are conditional on the fitted probe and a single encoder seed, with predictions fixed across resamples. Their width is therefore a lower bound on uncertainty from the full estimation pipeline; this limits conclusions based on whether the interval excludes zero.

criteria.effective_rank_improvement_rule: effective rank (RankMe): convolutional improves >=5% over next-best with 95% CI of the improvement above 5% (well-posed; baseline ~100).
criteria.note: The recorded hypothesis requires >=5% improvement over the next-best tokenizer in effective rank, R², and rank-IC. The relative threshold is well-defined for effective rank.
criteria.shuffled_reference_role: Shuffled embeddings provide a check for leakage and probe behavior: destroying embedding structure should produce a score near 0. They are not the baseline for evaluating the recorded criteria.
criteria.signal_rule: For each tokenizer and target, the encoder prediction score must exceed the manual-indicator baseline, which predicts the target from indicator variables. The paired day-block-bootstrap CI of (tokenizer - indicators) must exclude 0 in the tokenizer's favor. The absolute difference between convolutional and the next-best tokenizer is also reported for each target.

indicator_baseline.source: Manual-indicator baseline: RidgeCV predicts each target from the same indicator variables used to residualize the targets; each tokenizer is compared with this baseline.

training.description: Saved combined validation objective and training metadata. No per-epoch training-loss history or separate validation prediction loss is present.

corpus.note: all three tokenizer variants (linear / patch / convolutional) x 5 seeds were trained on this exact corpus
